clue.text: Musical chairs initially? Earl'd organised this children's game

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: letters that are organised get put into a fresh order
initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of chairs
the letters of Earl'd, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A nobleman has arranged a party with musical chairs to start the fun for the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical chairs' reads as one party game, but it splits: the musical is Cats, and 'chairs initially' supplies only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's cradle is the string game children play, looping a cord between their fingers into shapes.

clue.text: One who shows no emotion given raw cod, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an unfeeling, aloof person
second meaning, taken literally: uncooked chilled fish, with cod as an example

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for an unemotional person is read literally as chilled fish, and 'perhaps' flags cod as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An unresponsive, unfriendly person is idiomatically called this, while chilled uncooked cod literally fits the same two words.

clue.text: Last to expect mother turning up with father in Florida resort

indicators.note: last to a word means its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of expect

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother
PA is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A family waits for the parents to arrive, the last stop being a Florida holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city and resort on the Gulf coast of Florida, on Tampa Bay.

clue.text: Clandestine dockland garage needs sorting out

indicators.note: something that needs sorting out is in a muddle and must be put in a new order

parts.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A shady garage down by the docks needs a proper clean-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloak-and-dagger describes secretive spy-story intrigue, so it is an adjective for covert, clandestine activity.

clue.text: Bitter when with group under canvas?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: being under a covering means being enclosed by it, so one item sits within another

parts.note: 'under canvas' means camping, so canvas is a tent
a ring is a group, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: A wry question: does a group camping together turn sour?
explanation.walkthrough: The ring goes inside the tent, and AS goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent remarks are sharp and harsh, so the adjective serves as a synonym for bitter or caustic.

clue.text: Left in the morning with British essayist

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
a.m. marks morning hours
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A British writer of essays set off early one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British essayist' wants to be read as one unit, but British only supplies a letter; the definition is the essayist alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia and is one of the best-known English essayists.

clue.text: Old French artist almost returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so it is read right to left
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Edgar Degas, the French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An elderly French painter has nearly made it back home.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged is an adjective meaning elderly, matching old in sense and part of speech.

clue.text: Oppose profits being pocketed by fool

indicators.note: whatever is pocketed is tucked inside something else

parts.note: a goat is a silly person, as in 'acting the goat'
gains are profits

explanation.surface: Someone resists having their earnings taken by an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' as a goat comes from the phrase 'acting the goat'; the profits go in the middle, not at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: To go against something is a phrasal verb meaning to resist or oppose it.

clue.text: Withered, a dead butterfly

parts.note: withered plants are dry
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A shrivelled, lifeless butterfly, as found in a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: Most solvers know a dryad as a tree nymph, but it is also the name of a brown European butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: The dryad is a species of satyrid butterfly, so the insect name gives the word.

clue.text: A group of bishops reportedly praises religious song

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: lauds means praises, and in non-rhotic speech it matches the sound of the peers' title
a spiritual is a religious folk song

explanation.surface: A church choir's praise turns into a hymn about the bishops.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the r in the first word is silent, so the two words share a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lords Spiritual are the Church of England bishops who sit in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Dance with member next to ring

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A dance partner stands beside the boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbo is a Caribbean dance in which the dancer leans back to pass under a low bar.

clue.text: Portray me differently, short-term

indicators.note: doing something differently changes its arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An actor asks to be shown in a new light, at least for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporary describes something lasting only a limited time, a direct synonym of the adjective short-term.

clue.text: Statesman, outspoken Liberal, elected

parts.note: frank means candid, outspoken
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A politician, a plain-speaking Liberal, has won his seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Franklin was an American founding father, diplomat and statesman.

clue.text: Boy found hiding in fitted wardrobe

indicators.note: something hiding in a phrase sits concealed among its letters

parts.note: the end of fitted runs into the start of wardrobe

explanation.surface: A child playing hide-and-seek is discovered in the bedroom cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward is a boy's name, and crosswords often define a given name as boy or girl.

clue.text: Former PM (Welsh Duke?)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Duke of ... served as British Prime Minister
second meaning: the title by which Arthur Wellesley, victor of Waterloo, is known

explanation.walkthrough: Both meanings point to the same man, Arthur Wellesley; the parenthetical 'Welsh' with its question mark is a playful decoy, as he was not Welsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Wellesley, first Duke of Wellington, was both a famous general and a Tory Prime Minister.

clue.text: Anticipating signs, dunce goes out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are put in another order

parts.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A slow pupil reads the warning signs and leaves before trouble arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-guessing someone means predicting what they will do, so it can stand for anticipating.

clue.text: A good deal of opportunity to employ Arab coach

indicators.note: to employ is to take on, so one word takes another into itself
a good deal of something is most but not all of it, so the end is cut

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plenty of chances to hire an Arab horse for a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab coach' looks like the definition, but Arab is taken as written and coach alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old-fashioned open motor coach used for day trips and outings.

clue.text: Run through train

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to practise a play or speech before performing it
second meaning: to drill or coach someone by repeated practice

explanation.walkthrough: 'Run through train' suggests a railway, but both parts are verbs about practice.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise a performance and also to drill people in it, matching both verbs.

clue.text: Prudence, say, giving lucid narrative, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals an unexpected outcome, here an unexpected order of letters

parts.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A woman called Prudence turns out to be an unexpectedly clear storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: Prudence looks like a woman's name, but 'say' marks it as an example of a category.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is one of the four cardinal virtues, alongside justice, temperance and fortitude.

clue.text: Fruit in orchard's first row

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the first letter of orchard
a range is a row, as in a mountain range

explanation.surface: Fruit growing on the front row of trees in an orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange is a citrus fruit, so the general word fruit defines it by category.

clue.text: Love good article about king in newspaper

indicators.note: about means going round, so these letters wrap around another

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
G is the abbreviation for good
an is the indefinite article
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A romantic story about a king appears in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three pieces join and wrap around R after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a publication that speaks for a group, so a newspaper is an example of one.

clue.text: Hint supplied by close friend

definitions.meaning: first meaning, a verb: to suggest something indirectly
second meaning, a noun: a confidant

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the noun are spelt the same but pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to imply or suggest, and an intimate is a very close companion.

clue.text: Film star in part — not the eading character

indicators.note: not the leading character means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a factor is a part or element

explanation.surface: A movie star playing a role, though not the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The source prints 'eading' for 'leading' — fittingly, a word with its leading letter missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A film star is a performer in movies, and an actor is the general term for one.

clue.text: Little Seamus to speak about heroin

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round another

parts.note: to say is to speak
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Young Seamus is asked to talk about drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shay is a pet form of the Irish name Seamus, so it is what you might call him for short.

clue.text: Understood about odd Sherpa calling for ammunition

indicators.note: about means around, so one word encloses another

parts.note: 'I got it' means I understood

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange Himalayan guide is understood to be demanding weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sherpa is a Himalayan mountain guide; the rearranged letters sit inside GOT after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot is cannon ammunition made of small iron balls packed together like a bunch of grapes.

clue.text: Complete madman losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: nutter is British slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A total lunatic loses his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter is an adjective meaning complete or absolute, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: Pleasant French resort

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Riviera city on the Côte d'Azur

explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter is hidden by placing the place name second; the adjective and the city are spelt alike but pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice is an everyday synonym for pleasant and also the name of a resort city in southern France.

clue.text: Generally lighter round end of May (also end of April)

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one word goes around the others

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, used twice here for both months

parts.note: the last letter of May
and means also
the last letter of April

explanation.surface: The days get lighter from late spring onward, in general.
explanation.walkthrough: Lighter suggests brightness, but here it is a type of boat; BARGE surrounds the middle pieces after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: By and large is an idiom meaning on the whole, so it serves as a synonym for generally.
